reason: 'subequaling or shorter than the glume' compares the part with another named part: equality with another part (pattern 10), marked as approximate (pattern 01).

label: transversely ellipsoid
definition: A convex 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being ellipsoid with its longest axis perpendicular to the axis along which it is attached, so that it is broader than long. NOTE: PATO has ellipsoid only as a synonym of PATO:0000947 elliptic, which does not fix the orientation of the long axis; compare FLOPO:0991103 depressed.
reason: Used for anthers, ovaries, seeds and fruits that are wider than long. This is a fixed shape term, not ellipsoid plus an orientation of the whole part.

target: new: two values of one part (A-B compound)
reason: 'ovale-anguleux' means ovate in outline and angular: ovate (FLOPO:0991024) plus angular (PATO_0001977, synonym angulate) on the same petal. This is a compound of two values, not a new shape.
'Gousses à 1-2 articles' counts the segments of a loment (loment fruit PO_0030101). PO has no class for these segments, so this is a count of parts with the fruit as the container.
These are length measurements of the anther or stamen, taken including the connective appendage. The quality is length; the extent of the measured part stays in the record.
A comparison with a named part (the stamens): a relation to another part (pattern 09), with the stamen as the 'towards' part.
Negates PATO_0104032 coriaceous (synonym leathery), in the same way as 'unlobed'.

target: new: two values of one part (A-B compound)
reason: Covered with a mealy, wax-bearing powder: mealy (PATO_0104364, the earlier rule for farinose) plus waxy (PATO_0002384) on the same part. Two existing values together, not a new term.

Lobes that overlap one another, in the corolla or at the leaf base, are imbricate. The bearer is the set of lobes (pattern 16); 'to the right/left' is a detail of the aestivation that stays in the record.

target: new: two values of one part (A-B compound)
reason: Ovate in outline with a tail-like apex: ovate (FLOPO:0991024) for the bract plus caudate (PATO_0001880) for its apex. Two values, one of them on a sub-part.
Castaneous means chestnut-brown. 'Dark' is a degree of colour brightness and does not need its own term.

target: new: two values of one part (A-B compound)
reason: Pilose with hairs arising from papillae: papillose (FLOPO:0991059) plus pilose (FLOPO:0991048) on the same surface. Both values exist.
In grasses, conjugate racemes or spikes are two that arise together at the culm apex, a pair. This matches the definition of paired (synonym geminate).
A shape between linear (PATO_0001199) and oblong (PATO_0000946), written like 'linear-lanceolate': the continuum pattern between two values.
An equal-sided leaf base or blade has two similar halves on either side of the midrib: PATO symmetrical. It is the opposite of an oblique or inequilateral base.
An anther with many pollen sacs, more than the usual four: an indefinite count ('many') of pollen sac (PO_0025277) with the anther as the container.
Corolla lobes or lips that are nearly equal among themselves: the set quality equal, with 'sub' read as approximate (pattern 01).
Sulcate with a narrow groove. 'Narrowly' modifies the groove and needs no term; 'adaxially' or 'above' gives the surface of the bearer.
'Conforming to the endocarp' or 'terminal pinna conform' means like or fitting another part. This is a comparison whose second term is often missing, as with 'similar' in the earlier review.
Leaves or branchlets without a scent. PATO_0002191 aromatic is a molecular quality (aromatic ring), so the right negation is of odorous.
In Carex, sheath fronts that lack veins are veinless: vein (an exact synonym of vascular bundle) is absent. The spots in the same phrase are a separate statement.

label: caudex-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's resembling a caudex: short, thick, erect or ascending and often woody, persisting at the base of the plant. NOTE: Like FLOPO:0991325 rhizome-like; caudex itself is a synonym of stem PO:0009047.
reason: Floras use it for rhizomes and stems that are short, thick and erect, like a caudex. No PATO or FLOPO value covers this, and the 'X-like' form follows earlier classes.

An inflorescence whose flowers are crowded at the apex is condensed, as with the earlier rule for 'compact'. PATO_0001836 congested means a blocked opening and does not fit; 'apically' gives the region of the bearer.
Ambiguous between coral-red (of flowers) and coral-like branching (of hair tips and scales). PATO has no coral colour, and the sense depends on the bearer.
A faint pink colour over the part. 'Tinged' and '-ish' mark a weak or partial colour, which is approximate (pattern 01), not a new colour.
'Sepal same size as corolla tube' states equality with another part (pattern 10). Where it is said of a set of like parts, as with the subapical and apical teeth, it is FLOPO:0991102 equal.
Negates the existing value tuberculate.
Cystoliths sit in lithocysts. FLOPO_0986068 lithocyst already carries the cystolith readings in the allowed combinations, so this is presence of that part. 'Densely' is a degree.

target: new: two values of one part (A-B compound)
reason: Bristles set in a comb-like row along the margin: setose (PATO_0002289) plus pectinate (FLOPO:0991033) on the same margin. Two existing values.
Negates the existing value inflexed (Latin 'haud inflexis' included).
